args.body: PARTLY EVALUATED: 1 of the 2 checks could not be run at all -- lift_carries_the_weight (the question asked is about POWERED flight, and this check cannot answer it. It compares lift with weight at a given airspeed, which is an area question; powered flight is a power question -- whether the flight muscle can supply the induced and profile power through a wingbeat, continuously, at that animal's mass. That needs a coefficient measured through a wingbeat and a muscle power density for the clade, and this repository has neither.). The checks that did run found no contradiction, and a check that did not run is not a check that passed. The flight branch refuses, and the refusal is the right one: the question asked is about POWERED flight, and this check cannot answer it. It compares lift with weight at a given airspeed, which is an area question; powered flight is a power question -- whether the flight muscle can supply the induced and profile power through a wingbeat, continuously, at that animal's mass. That needs a coefficient measured through a wingbeat and a muscle power density for the clade, and this repository has neither.

lift.limiting_factor: the question asked is about POWERED flight, and this check cannot answer it. It compares lift with weight at a given airspeed, which is an area question; powered flight is a power question -- whether the flight muscle can supply the induced and profile power through a wingbeat, continuously, at that animal's mass. That needs a coefficient measured through a wingbeat and a muscle power density for the clade, and this repository has neither.

detail.why_this_is_correct: The repository holds exactly two measured maximum lift coefficients: a stuffed Cypselurus hiraii and a live Petaurus breviceps. An insect at Re of order 100 with a flapping wing is aerodynamically unlike both -- unsteady, with leading-edge vortex lift that a steady coefficient does not represent at all. Returning a number here by borrowing one of the two would be exactly the failure this layer was built to stop.

result.scope: A co-design log. Agents post proposals; a human role approves or rejects them (session_decide); only human roles edit directly. Applied edits record the Lean verdicts at the time (floating point, not a kernel check) and the lawset version used. Authors are role labels, not people.
